for the record 
POINTS WEST - Well, we saw Elvis emerge in the fabulous 50s, watched with dismay 
and then awe as the Beatles led the vanguard of the new rock of the 60s, and now, as 
1974 draws to to close we will all soon be witness to the latest dance craze to sweep 
America and perhaps herald the arrival of the next BIG star, Tom Seufert. Who? 
Seufert is not to be trifled with my friend, nor his new Epic single "Casablanca Belly 
Roll." Complete with a snake charmer, shiek and belly dancer (who unfortunately 
wasn't either Little Egypt or Fatima), Tommy and producer Dave Kirshenbaum 
displayed the new product at our popular Sunset Blvd. offices before an astounded 
staff. What shook everybody up so much was the impact the disk had - 
I mean, Manu 
Dibango, look out! We've got a record here. It's got Hollywood in a frenzy and when 
that happens, can Ames, Iowa be far behind. 
"The Phantom of the Paradise," after a long series of legal delays, finally debuted in 
Hollywood (Oct. 31). With music by the film's star, Paul Williams, the comedic horror 
flick runs the gamut of tongue in cheek industry one liners while providing an up - 
tempo story line of music and mayhem. Jeffrey Commanor and Keith Allison play 
cameo roles, while William Finley plays the elusive Phantom ... Lee Radziwill was 
spotted at the Marvin Gaye concert at Radio City Music Hall in the Big Apple (NY) 
boogieing like mad with Robert Stigwood and Andy Warhol - soul is where you find it 
... Andy Kim is in L.A. working on the follow up single to his recent #1 smash, "Rock 
Me Gently." 
Iron Butterfly will soar into Paramount studios to cut their first LP with MCA starting 
this week with all new material. The eyes and ears of the world will be tuned in for the 
results of those sessions to see if the magic of "Inna Gadda Da Vida" is still there. 
Check us in January for the results ... David Gates, former lead singer of Bread will 
be Al Schlessinger's special guest Nov. 3 at the Sherwood Oaks Experimental Col- 
lege. Apparently the series of lectures is going quite well and generating con- 
siderable interest. Where was it when I was slaving away in History 235 at Syracuse? 
Enjoyed a fascinating talk with veteran studio engineer Lee Kiefer, particularly his 
anecdotes about the various hits he's tracked. Recently, while taking a break around 
5:00 o'clock in the a.m. at a record plant session, Lee and the "artist" shared a couple 
of drinks to relax, then said artist solo'd into the studio, sat behind the keyboards and 
in one take knocked out a thing called "Nothing From Nothing Leaves Nothing." Billy 
Preston, natch, and Lee says it was a bit of magic. "We never intended really doing 
anything, just kind of filling up time when Billy did his thing. First take, too, and his 
foot tappin' against the piano gave us the guide for the background laid down later on. 
Tom Seutert (behind Fatima) Bellies Up 
You can hear that foot tapping on the record," Lee says, "if you listen closely." 
Of the more than 1000 LPs I've reviewed this year (so far) for Cash Box, perhaps 
the most exciting and rewarding one has been "The Gregg Allman Tour" featuring 
Boyer & Talton along with a 24 piece orchestra backing Gregg. I've mentioned the 
cuts I dig in the album review section, but I feel compelled to praise Gregg for going 
out on his own not only to tour, but to make (with the invaluable assistance of Johnny 
Sandlin) such a fine record. In my estimation it rivals "Live Rhymin' " for "in studio" 
quality which is remarkable considering the much funkier music that's dealt with on 
this two record set. Most bands and probably individuals would have folded up after 
sustaining losses like Gregg did with the death of his brother Duane and bassist Berry 
Oakley, but Gregg Allman's a proud man and should be singled out for extraordinary 
merit and praise for carrying a tremendous load on his shoulders and doing it with 
such soul and dignity. Sure, the Stones are greatest, but Gregg, my hat's off to you 
and I'm sure all the folks at Capricorn and in Macon are every bit as proud as I am of 
this superb new LP. 
Dave Loggins, while doing a series of college dates with Jim Stafford became 
friendly with the "Spiders and Snakes" man and the two have decided to collaborate 
on a number of tunes and hopefully an LP. Which label, Epic or MGM, will get it is still 
up in the air, but it sounds like a great team ... Booker T. Jones has his new band 
ready and will be out on the road in November playing some oldies like "Green 
Onions" and some of his great new material culled from his "Evergreen" LP released 
two weeks ago. Booker's fantastic and his professionalism never gets in the way of his 
idealism though the two do go nicely together ... One of Epic's hot new acts, Honk, 
as a part of its upcoming tour, will open for Poco and Loggins & Messina, Dec. 14 in 
L.A. I always did believe in the sink or swim principal myself. 
The late Wes Montgomery's brother, Monk, who is currently touring Africa, intends 
to start a "bring jazz to Las Vegas" campaign when he gets back. Hope it works ... 
Donovan's first west coast dates in over two years will take place in Berkeley Dec. 8, 
Santa Monica Civic (11) and San Diego (12) ... Dan Fogelberg recently sold out six 
consecutive dates at Denver's Ebbets Field ... Minnie Riperton returning to L.A. after 
being feted with a parade and dinner with the mayor of her hometown, Gainesville, 
Georgia ... Johnny Nash and the Isley Bros. will appear at the L.A. Sports Area (Nov. 
15) three days after Harold Melvin & The Blue Notes return to the Total Experience. 
david budge 
EAST COASTINGS -Well, another week of action has come and gone and I'm here to 
do my best to report the Apple action right from the core I'm sure ... So much for in- 
ternal rhyme ... well anyone who may have guessed at Ringo's new Apple single will 
be pleased to know that it is "Only You" and features among other luminaries brother 
John Lennon and another John by the name of Elton ... it seems that when Ringo 
cuts any disk the studio turns into a superstar jamboree and stars as those just men- 
tioned as well as Billy Preston and others show their faces and really brighten up the 
recording sessions ... Ringo's LP is due for a mid -November release and it will be fun 
to see who turns up on the LP and who is in on the sessions ... 2,220 tickets were 
sold out in only two hours when hundreds of ticket buyers, eager to see Jerry Garcia's 
first performance since the disbanding of the Grateful Dead recently, beseiged New 
York's Bottom Line. 75 Garcia freaks camped out Last Monday night, October 28 to 
be first in line when the box office opened Tuesday, October 29 at 1:00 PM. Garcia is 
slated to perform November 5-7 with Merle Saunders ... interestingly enough no ad- 
vertising was used to announce Garcia's opening; the Bottom Line announced his up- 
coming appearance at the club last Friday evening, included him on their coming at- 
tractions telephone tape, and posted signs outside the club and in the box office win- 
dow ... the once lead singer of the Young Rascal's Eddie Brigati, has been signed to 
the Elektra label ... a retraction on Ellie Greenwich ... the way I worded her Birthday 
juxtaposed to Al Jolson dying it appeared that the lovely lady had suffered some ter- 
minal illness also ... my apologies to Ellie and her friends for the mistake, but the 
pressures of deadline can do strange things to one's wording ... there was a jam be- 
tween Richard Betts and the Charlie Daniels band with special guest picks including 
the likes of Richard Betts on guitar, Toy Caldwell on steel guitar, Jerry Eubanks on 
saxophone, and Paul Riddle on drums all from the Marshall Tucker band ... Sam Mc- 
Pherson played mouth harp and Artimus Pyle plays conga drums and Jamie Nichol on 
conga drums ... there will be a special EP issued with the LP billed as Volunteer Jam 
'74 it was recorded live at the War Memorial Auditorium in Nashville and promises to 
be one hell of an album ... the album is shipping the beginning of November and will 
be titled "Fire On The Mountain" and the Charlie Daniels band cooks because they 
are hotter than ever ... Supergroup Chicago wound its final tour of the season with 
advance sellout concerts at Nassau Coliseum and Madison Square Garden. I had the 
pleasure of seeing the group at the Garden and they put on a very fine performance 
. this tour was the largest grossing swing through the United States ever of the 
Columbia Records band, which sold out most of its engagements well in advance ... 
the Garden was one of the places that the group used closed circuit television as well 
as the LA Forum and Chicago Stadium and it seems that they will use this system for 
their 1975 concert dates ... "Chicago VIII" album is due for a late November release, 
and the band will start recording material for a next album early in 1975... Columbia 
group American Tears will be touring with Alvin Lee sometime soon ... the Stones 
Chicago 
are being booked for a tour in the summer of 1975... that should be something to 
really see ... Burton Cummings who is lead singer of the Guess Who, and new 
guitarist Dom Troiano, have co -written the next album for th RCA group called 
"Flavors" ... it is due for a January release date ... "I hardly listen to rock music," ad- 
mits Robin Trower, qualifying that by adding "I Like the Rolling Stones, and I used to 
like Cream, and of course Jimi Hendrix" ... Danny Fogelberg has come up with a new 
country -rock album called "Souvenirs" ... Richard Chamberlain, an old pal of Elton 
John, took off on a Hawaiian vacation, and met up with the Rocket Man himself in 
Honolulu ... Minnie Riperton who taped an ABC-TV "In Concert" show, had such per- 
sonal friends on hand as Cat Stevens, Ringo Starr and Chris Stainton ... "I never liked 
being nothing," admits Ian Hunter of Mott The Hoople, explaining why he wanted to 
be a rock and roll star ... here we go by way of a retraction ... MCS Enterprises 
wishes to sincerely offer their thanks to all those who responded to their plea in Cash 
Box, for help on a fund raising concert plan for MDAA. Due to technical problems 
with MDAA, we have been unable to continue with our plans. Sincerest apologies to 
those who have already offered their time and help to us ... Fleetwood Mac's ex - 
manager Clifford Davis has halted the British release of their latest LP, "Heroes Are 
Hard To Find," as retaliation for Fleetwood's court injunction against Davis for 
promoting concerts by a group called Fleetwood Mac and having nothing to do with 
the real group ... Country Hams, featuring Chet Atkins, Floyd Cramer, and Jeff Britten 
recorded a single entitled "Walking In The Park With Eloise." It was written 20 years 
ago by James McCartney, Paul's father. The record was produced by Paul McCartney 
during his recent stay in Nashville ... Michael D'Albuquerque has resigned as bass 
player for the Electric Light Orchestra ... he will be replaced by Mike Groucott .. 
when Bonnie Raitt played the Orpheum Theater in Boston she was on the bill with 
blues legends Sippie Wallace and Roosevelt Sykes and up came Jr. Wells and his en- 
tire band what a night that must have been!! ... Stevie Wonder jammed with Graham 
Central Station at Paul's Mall ... the Beach Boys are at the Caribou Ranch recording a 
new LP and Brian has written a slew of new tunes following on the heels of their gold 
love album ... The Beau Brummels remember them?? are recording under the 
production of Ted Templeman ... Arlo Gutherie and Pete Seeger will be coming out 
with a live album recorded during their string of concerts ... new Carlin LP will be out 
in November and it is called "Toledo Window Box" ... Sid 1 Cut 1 is a track called 
"Goofy Shit" which Carlin uses to define his societal role ... Mott is coming out with a 
live LP recorded at the Uris Theater during the days of Ariel Bender and Mott has 
recorded a new single called "The Saturday Night Gigs" which was released three 
weeks ago and spotlights Mick Ronson on lead guitar .. . 
Until next week ...

The Jazz Composers Orchestra Association 
The problems of creating a small in- 
dependent record label devoted to 
quality music are well-known. Limited by 
moderate audience interest and insuf- 
ficient funds for promotion, the indies 
are often overpowered by the facilities of 
the large conglomerates. One indepen- 
dent organization that has managed to 
succeed in spite of generally hard 
economic times and the pressures from 
more secure firms is the Jazz Composers 
Orchestra Association. 
Originally devoted to giving free 
public concerts and workshops for com- 
posers interested in writing extended 
works for large jazz orchestra, the non- 
profit JCOA has formed a record label 
which has released three major pieces 
stemming from those workshops: 
Michael Mantler's "The Jazz Composer's 
Orchestra," Carla Bley's "Escalator Over 
The Hill," and Don Cherry's "Relativity 
Suite." 
From the onset, JCOA sought to 
distribute their own records. The music 
is one of the primary examples of jazz' 
avant-garde and its creative cutting - 
edge. Though the initial number of 
buyers was small, the listening 
population grew at a rapid rate. As a 
result, the New Music Distribution Ser- 
vice was created and within two years, 
the service has taken on consignment 
and resold some 80,000 LP's of imported 
and domestic jazz work. NMDS has 
recently added 40 albums on 23 labels to 
the catalogue, bringing the total listings 
to 275 albums on 67 musician operated 
companies. 
The music handled by the Association. 
now extends beyond the jazz field. 
Ethnic music and modern "classics" are 
among the varied mediums distributed. 
The only qualification the JCOA makes 
in accepting new records is that the 
recordings be examples of "the new 
music." Pop and folk are not handled 
because the organization believes that 
mass -market music is better handled by 
commercial distributors. 
Even though the NMDS has suc- 
ceeded in the past, the service is finding 
it difficult to continue its progress within 
the tighter economic structure. The 
profits from JCOA Records, in fact, are 
turned into the main source of expen- 
ditures for the distribution service. JCOA 
is trying to advertise NMDS' records 
through an internal promotion campaign. 
The second edition of "Corrective News 
Distribution," a service newsletter, is 
being prepared by Carla Bley. Ad- 
ditionally, a press release on the 40 new 
albums acquired for distribution is being 
sent to all the standard sales outlets. 
Bill Ewell of JCOA explained the sim- 
ple economics of the Association. Both 
the JCOA and NMDS are non-profit 
organizations, he said, and added that 
the former receives money from the New 
York State Council of the Arts for their 
workshops. All other activities, such as 
distribution and pressing of the records, 
are funded through private grants and 
profits from the first three JCOA albums, 
he remarked. 
Actively engaged in the difficult 
process of raising money in a depressed 
market, the JCOA has recently received 
a grant from "The Martha Baird 
Rockefeller Fund for Music." The money 
has been allocated for the expansion and 
development of the distribution service, 
Ewell explained. He said that a person 
was added to the staff to boost new ac- 
counts and, hopefully, increase the 
fundings. If, he emphasized, the JCOA 
had a person to handle the business af- 
fairs, then they could release another in- 
dividual for distribution. The cash flow 
from NMDS' more established com- 
panies - JCOA, Watt, Strata -East, CRI 
and PM Records - is a solid source of in- 
come for day to day activities, Ewell said. 
The problem for all independent com- 
panies, Ewell concluded, is that more 
time is needed for expansion. However, 
tight money limits the personnel who can 
be released for the most important ac- 
tivity: distribution, he said. 
steven marks 
STANLEY'S THE MAN - Stanley Turren - 
tine is shown surrounded by fans and 
autographing copies of his first Fantasy 
album, "Pieces Of Dreams," during an 
engagement at Chicago's Jazz 
Showcase. At extreme left is Rudy Run- 
nels, program director at WBMX, 
Chicago. 
BELL INKS GIL SCOTT -HERON - Gil Scott -Heron has been signea to the Bell group 
this week, announced Clive Davis, the label's president. 
Gil Scott -Heron, only 25, is an accomplished poet and songwriter. His first two 
albums, on Flying Dutchman, included "Home Is Where The Hatred Is," "Lady Day 
And John Coltrane," and "The Revolution Will Not Be Televised," which has become 
a black rallying cry. More recently, Scott -Heron's album "Winter In America," was 
propelled by the single, "The Bottle." 
all that's jazz 
picks of the week 
CIRCLE/PARIS - CONCERT - Anthony Brax- 
ton, Chick Corea, David Holland, and Barry Alt- 
schul - ECM 1018/19 ST 
One of the best performed ad most cohesive 
jazz albums recently released. Though a com- 
bination of solos and duets for the most part, the 
album somehow remains extremely unified. It 
demands serious listening, but the enjoyment is 
well worth the effort. On Wayne Shorter's 
"Nefertiti," Corea opens the piece with a har- 
monic introduction. Then both he and Braxton 
develope changes to the popular melody, 
enough snatches of which are present to keep 
the listener oriented. Dave Holland's bass solo is 
a rhythmic tour de force, consisting of multi - 
octave leaps and changes of rhythm. 
SORCERY - Jack DeJonette - Prestige P10081 
Jack DeJonette's third album as a leader. "Sor- 
cery" is a combination of solos based upon a 
highly rhythmic theme first announced by Dave 
Holland's bass and then repeated at various in- 
tervals throughout the piece. John Abercrom- 
bie's guitar chorus reminds one of the guitar 
work done in the late '60's by the Jazz Com- 
posers Orchestra. Of interest, too, is Bennie 
Maupin's bass clarinet solo, which seems to tran- 
scend the limits of the instrument's range. 
"Reverend King Suite" is an interesting com- 
bination of sounds and textures reminiscent of 
Carla Bley's "Tong Funeral." 
BLACK BEINGS - Frank Lowe - ESP 3013 
A devotional album, in John Coltrane's sense 
of the word, dedicated to the "musicians who 
gave their all." Side A consists of Lowe's exten- 
sive "In Trane's Name." The piece is an 
emotional powerhouse. The free -blowing music 
typical of Coltrane's middle -to -later works (see 
"Ascension") is based upon a combination of 
solos and dialogues by Lowe on tenor sax and 
Joseph Jarman of the Art Ensemble of Chicago 
on sop and alto sax. The sax dialogues utilize the 
two instruments Coltrane made his own, yet ex- 
tend the bounds of his performances. The piece 
does not exist in time, but explodes as a spatial 
wonder. 
THE PHIL WOODS QUARTET - Phil Woods - 
Testament T-4402 
Phil Woods' sound is an interesting synsthesis 
of music's development from the late '40's to the 
present. At times, it is a tightly structured com- 
bination of two melody lines emphasizing rhyth- 
mic and harmonic variation (on "Yesterdays," for 
instance, though Woods occasionally lapses into 
some perfunctory arpeggio scales). At other 
times, the music works a freer form. Time sig- 
natures are varied, electronics are utilized, and 
choruses only appear connected to the melody 
by the requirements of intervallic logic (see 
"Nefertiti" and "Riot"). 
IT COULD ONLY HAPPEN WITH YOU - Duke 
Pearson - Blue Note - LA 3176 
A combination of Latin rhythms and sensuous 
bossa nova jazz. Flora Purim's vocals, especially 
on "It Could Only Happen," and "Stormy," are 
husky and earthy, and possess a remarkable 
range and timbre. Note the interaction of her 
voice and the tenor sax on "Round and Round." 
Pearson's piano solo during the first paraphrase 
of "Emily" is a controlled manipulation of the 
main theme which explores some interesting 
rhythmic changes before depositing the listener 
back in the lap of the melody. 
LEONARD FEATHER PRESENTS THE EN- 
CYCLOPEDIA OF JAZZ, VOL. 5 - MCA 2-4063 
A musical counterpart of "The Encyclopedia of 
Jazz" covering the period of the '50's. The 
various sounds and textures include post -bop 
developments, the big band (Doc Severinson is 
heard on a cut with Sal Salvador's band) and 
"cool" jazz. The avant-garde is noticeable by 
their absence. Tony Scott and The All -Stars 
"Lester Leaps On" revolves around the bass 
work of Oscar Pettiford. George Wallington's 
guitar solo suggests the direction later guitarists 
will take. Coleman Hawkins' variation of "Body 
and Soul" originally recorded in 1939 is a rhap- 
sodic joy to behold.

cash box R&D news report 
r&b ingredients 
Barry White announced the addition of a creative department to his music produc- 
tion companies, and the appointment of Bernie Butler to head up the newly formed 
operation. Operating under the umbrella of Barr-Larr Inc., the primary purpose of the 
creative department under the direction of Mr. Butler, will be to handle the 
operations and merchandise of the newly formed "Maestro Barry White Fan Club," 
that launches its initial membership drive and kick-off campaign during the month of 
November. Barry White has also contracted the services of Warren Lanier Enterprises 
Public Relations Agency, to work hand in hand with Bernie Butler, to publicize and 
promote the special projects associated with Barry Whites production companies and 
the creative department. Barry, Love Unlimited, and the Love Unlimited Orchestra left 
Los Angeles Nov. 4 for a month long concert tour that will cover the East Coast in- 
cluding dates at New York's Felt Forum, the New Haven Coliseum and the Toledo 
Sports Arena. Barry White, Love Unlimited and the Love Unlimited Orchestra will 
also be making a guest appearance on "The Midnight Special" on Friday, Nov. 15. 
Barry will host the Eric Burdon Band and others as part of his hectic November 
schedule ... O'Jays' Eddie Levert recently became the father of a baby girl. His wife, 
Martha, presented him with the eight pound, nine ounce infant in Warrensville, Ohio 
at the Brentwood Hospital. The baby has been named Kandice Nicole ... The Ohio 
Players' "Skin Tight" LP sold 13,000 units last week continuing the fantastic success 
of that very popular group ... Following their engagement at Hollywood's Whiskey 
Au Go Go, The Younghearts, male vocal group on 20th Century Records, filled a 
week-end engagement at The Apartment nitery of Los Angeles and then flew to 
Portland, Oregon for a series of concerts and appearances. Their current single 
"Wake Up and Start Standing" from their current album "A Taste of the Younghearts" 
is moving nationwide and might become the biggest record to date for the group. At 
the Whiskey they were backed by the Mean Machine and tore through a great set, in- 
cluding their single and a great arrangement of Stevie Wonder's "You Are The Sun- 
shine of My Life." The crowd loved their smooth vocal style and slick but restrained 
stage presence ... Hosea Williams, national soul promotion director of 20th Century 
Records, is back in Los Angeles following a product promotion tour that covered 
Chicago, Cleveland, Detroit, Philadelphia and New York ... Ahmad Jamal and trio 
from Playboy Club in Denver, Colorado to The Smiling Dog Nite Club in Cleveland, 
Ohio ... David Ruffin's opening at the Whiskey was a merry time for all. Norman Whit- 
field came from out of the audience to lead the band for a number and David did some 
of the biggest hits with the Temptations including "Losing You," "I Wish It Would 
Rain" and "Smiling Faces" besides some new tunes from his new Motown LP, "Me 
and Rock 'n' Roll Are Here To Stay." His six man back-up band gave him solid support 
and Ruffin proved he was back in the big time ... Hodges, James and Smith, 20th 
Century Records female vocal group to tour the Philippine Islands during Nov. and 
Dec. 
Billy Cobham, Atlantic Records artist, will be making a big east coast engagemer 
when he headlines at the Avery Fisher Hall in New York City on Monday, Nov. 11 
Cobham has just finished recording his third Atlantic album entitled "Total Eclipse,' 
slated for release in late November ... Stan Lewis, president of Jewel/Paula 
Records, announced the latest rhythm and blues release "Baby (You Know I'm Gonna 
Miss You) Pt. 1" by the Montclairs ... Capitol ships two new Haven Records singles 
this week - Gene Redding's "(We've Got) More Than It Takes," produced and 
penned by Lambert and Potter, from Redding's "Blood Brother" album and Margo 
Thunder's "Expressway To Your Heart," a remake of the Gamble and Huff hit for the 
Soul Survivors. Lambert and Potter produced the single for 14 year -old Thunder... 
Doug Morris and Dick Vanderbilt of Big Tree Records, distributed by Atlantic, an- 
nounced the signing of Hot Chocolate and Dennis Roussos. Hot Chocolate, a popular 
English R&B group, authored "Brother Louie" and their album "Cicero Park" is due 
for release. Roussos sang lead for Aphrodite's Child and is currently a favorite on the 
Continent ... Philly Groove recording artists The Finishing Touch have released their 
first single "Second Best (Is Never Enough)" ... ABC/Blue Thumb recording artists 
The Crusaders were at a recent autograph signing appearance at Tower Records. 
Hundreds came to chat and get free T-shirts and balloons ... Singer Freda Payne will 
headline a benefit concert for the United Black College Fund at Houston's Civic 
Auditorium, Nov. 24 ... The Inner City Cultural Center of Los Angeles has published 
the premiere issue of "Neworld," a magazine centering around the arts ... Capitol 
recording artists Tavares will appear with comedian Bill Cosby at the Circle Star 
Theater in San Carlos, California, Nov. 15-17 ... Soulville recording artists The 
Sound Experience are set for concert dates in Philadelphia, at the Astro Disc Club and 
Lincoln University, during the month of November ... Philly Groove female trio The 
First Choice are continuing to hold a strong following on the disco level throughout 
the country with tunes off their new LP "The Players" while their single of the same 
name climbs up the charts.

Mayfield Starts New 
LP While `Mimi' Waits 
HOLLYWOOD - Curtis Mayfield, his 
starring role in the motion picture "Mimi" 
pushed back until next spring, is now 
writing material for his next album, a fol- 
low-up to "Sweet Exorcist." 
The Curtom Records star was to have 
also written the score for "Mimi," but 
Columbia Pictures pushed back the star- 
ting date until early 1975. Film will be 
shot in New Orleans, as an updated 
remake of the opera "La Boheme." 
Mayfield is working out of the Curtom 
studios in Chicago, according to 
executive Mary Stuart. 
°'Jays In Studio 
Completing Album 
HOLLYWOOD - Philadelphia Inter- 
national recording stars the O'Jays, com- 
posed of Eddie Levert, Walter Williams, 
and William Powell, are in the process of 
completing their newest LP tentatively 
titled "The Law." 
The album, which is scheduled for 
release at the beginning of the year, is 
produced by Gamble and Huff and ar- 
ranged by Bobby Martin. The LP is being 
recorded at the Sigma Sound Studios in 
Philadelphia, with the MFSB Orchestra 
accompanying the O'Jays. 
Tunes featured on the album include 
"Just Don't Seem To Be My Day," "Just 
Let Me Love You," and "What Am 
I 
Waiting For" by Bunny Sigler, who 
penned such O'Jay songs as "Sunshine" 
and "When The World's At Peace." Pro- 
ducers Gamble and Huff wrote "Can't 
Nobody Break Us Up," "The Rich Get 
Richer and The Poor Get Poorer," "How 
Time Flies," and "Living In The Boun- 
daries Of The Law" (the title tune) for the 
album. 
The new LP release will mark the fifth 
collaboration of the O'Jays with the Gam- 
ble and Huff producing team. 
"Live In London," the O'Jays' current 
album release, has just been certified 
gold, signifying album sales have 
reached the one million dollar mark. 
The trio is currently rehearsing for 
their headline appearance at the famed 
Waldorf-Astoria Hotel's Empire Room in 
New York City. 
"Zaire '74" Crew 
Finishes Filming 
HOLLYWOOD - Eight camera crews 
have concluded filming for "Zaire '74," 
which includes a music festival that 
features such performers as the Pointer 
Sisters, the Crusaders, Hugh Masekela, 
James Brown, B. B. King and many 
others. 
In addition to the music festival, the 
camera crews also shot 19 hours of film 
on the country of Zaire, and the events 
leading to the championship fight be- 
tween Muhammad Ali and George Fore- 
man. 
Leon Gast is in charge of editing for 
the film, which will be released early in 
1975. 
Crusaders & Pointers 
Set For Japan Tour 
HOLLYWOOD - Two top American 
acts, The Crusaders and the Pointer 
Sisters, have been signed to perform in 
Japan for the first time. They will tour 
that country briefly as of mid -November. 
The instrumental group and the vocal 
group will give a joint recital on Nov. 15 
at Nakano Sun Plaza Hall, according to 
UOP, which is promoting the show. 
The Crusaders last concert was at the 
Zaire Festival, while the Pointers 
headlined a recent European concert 
tour, then performed at the Grand Ole 
Opry in Nashville. 
Latest album for The Crusaders is 
"Southern Comfort," distributed by ABC 
Records. 
Sister Sledge Signs HHV 
HOLLYWOOD - Sister Sledge has 
signed for exclusive worldwide publicity 
and public relations with Hecht Harman 
Vukas Creative Communications, Inc. 
Consisting of four young girls, Sister 
Sledge is the only girl group currently 
signed with Atlantic Records. Their first 
single, "Love Don't You Go Through No 
Changes," set for a Nov. 1 release, was 
arranged by Bert Decoteaux and 
produced by Tony Sylvester. 
HOT SOUL EXPLOSION - A pre- 
planning meeting for the Atlantic/ATCO 
"soul explosion" campaign involving 10 
of Atlantic's artists, and also a pre - 
strategy meeting on Gene Page's new 
LP "Hot City" were held in New York 
recently. Attending the meeting were, 
from left to right: Bill Staton (east coast 
special projects,) Sonny Woods (regional 
mgr. -south), Clarence Bullard (local NY 
promotion), Gary Johnson (regional 
mgr. -east coast), Henry Allen (vice- 
president for R&B product), Paul John- 
son (national promotion director for 
R&B), Tommy Phillips (west coast 
manager-R&B), Eddie Holland (regional 
mgr. -mid -west), and Alan Lott (director 
of album product.) 
FOR ART'S SAKE - Shown at the very 
first Blue Note Records "Jazz for Art's 
Sake" mini -concert held at Alan McKen- 
zie-Watson's photo studio in Los Angeles 
are (from left) Eddie Levine, head of 
promotion for Blue Note; Bobby Hut- 
cherson, who appeared at the Art's Sake 
concert; George Butler, general 
manager for the UA -distributed jazz 
label; famed jazz journalist Leonard 
Feather, who led a discussion of the 
music and jazz in general after the con- 
cert; and producer Keg Johnson, co- 
producer of Gene Harris' recent Blue 
Note album "Astralsignal." 
COOL WATERS - Everybody's all smiles 
as Waters signs with Blue Note Records, 
the first vocal group ever signed to the 
prestigious 35 -year -old jazz label. 
Shown surrounding Al Teller, president 
of United Artists Records, who distribute 
Blue Note, are (from left) Keg Johnson, 
producer of Waters; Maxine Waters; 
George Butler, general manager of Blue 
Note; Luther Waters; Oren Waters; Julia 
Waters and Judith Dornstein of UA's 
legal department. 
Hancock's "Death 
Wish" Released 
HOLLYWOOD - Herbie Hancock's 
soundtrack album for the film "Death 
Wish" has been released by Columbia 
Records, though the picture has been 
out for some time. 
David Rubinson produced the record. 
Hancock's latest album on Columbia is 
his "Thrust" LP, a follow-up to his big - 
selling "Headhunters" record.

h box editorial 
`Greatest Hits' As 
Great Sellers 
In these days of spiralling costs, stagnation, and recession, records remain 
one of the cheapest and most accessible forms of entertainment, making them 
the perfect gifts for the holiday buying season. 
The "Greatest Hits" album, traditionally a popular gift giving item, once 
again looks to be one of the approaches labels will be keying on for strong 
sales. These albums, which are usually in the form of studio or "live" versions 
of previously released material, have also proven helpful in stimulating the 
sales of artists' catalogs. 
Released in just the last two weeks have been live recordings by Gregg 
Allman, David Bowie, the Four Tops, Fairport Convention, the Marshall 
Tucker Band, Mott the Hoople, and Frank Sinatra - all containing previously 
released material. "Greatest Hits" albums of studio material have been 
marketed by groups and artists like Elton John, the Moody Blues, the 
Partridge Family, Jan and Dean, Bobby Womack, B.J. Thomas, Dionne 
Warwick, Bobby Goldsboro and Billy "Crash" Craddock. 
This is in addition to studio or live "Greatest Hits" albums which are already 
charted by the Beach Boys ("Endless Summer") and Crosby, Stills, Nash & 
Young (both former #1 LPs on the Cash Box charts), Jim Croce, the Pointer 
Sisters, Emerson, Lake and Palmer, the O'Jays, Santana, Bread, Marvin Gaye, 
Rory Gallagher, John Denver, Nitty Gritty Dirt Band, Duane Allman, and Alice 
Cooper. 
The trend has apparently also carried over to the jazz field as evidenced by 
CTI Records' "Baddest" series which comprises previously released material 
culled from albums by Stanley Turrentine and Freddie Hubbard. ABC has 
released "John Coltrane - The Greatest Years Vol. III" and has added to the 
"Impulse Years" series, two record sets featuring material by Elvin Jones, Milt 
Jackson, and Duke Ellington. 
With "live" albums promised by artists like Joni Mitchell, Cat Stevens, 
Argent, and Brian Auger, and "Greatest Hits" collections by Andy Kim, the 
Turtles, Rick Nelson, the Ventures, Paul Anka, the Hollies, and Jay and the 
Americans due for release imminently, all indications point to another holiday 
season of good sales catalyzed by the strength of the "Greatest Hits" LP.

IT'S ONLY ROCK & ROLL

cash box/album reviews 
THE WHO - A QUICK ONE/SELL OUT - The 
Who - Producer: Kit Lambert MCA2-4067 
One of two great two -fers capsulizing a signifi- 
cant portion of the early who years, this 
particular set reaches back to the days of "Happy 
Jack," "Run Run Run," "Boris The Spider," "So 
Sad About Us," "Armenia City In The Sky," 
"Odorono," "Our Love Was, Is," "I Can See For 
Miles," "Tattoo" and "Medac." This was the era 
before "Tommy" and "Quadrophenia" and 
reflects the brilliance of four men who have en- 
dured the ravages of superstardom and along 
with the Stones, remain intact. 
THE SILVER FOX - Charlie Rich - Producer: 
Billy Sherrill - Epic PE 33250 
The entertainer of the year, or as this LP calls 
him, the silver fox, once again places himself at 
the very top of an elite circle of superstars with 
this captivating LP, one that features five brand 
new tunes in addition to some previously re- 
corded, but beautifully rendered vintage Rich 
material including a medley entitled "Rondo a la 
Charlie." Among the great new tunes displayed 
adroitly here are "I Love My Friend", "Pieces Of 
My Life" and "Your Place Is Here With Me." 
PAUL ANKA GOLD - Paul Anka - Sire 
SASH -3704-2 
The Paul Anka story is depicted beautifully on 
this deluxe two record set that contains no less 
than 28 of the singing sensation's finest tunes. 
Remember "Diana"? Well it kicks this set off to a 
nostalgic start and the hits just keep rolling on, 
including "You Are My Destiny," "Puppy Love," 
"Lonely Boy," "Dance On Little Girl," "Hello, 
Young Lovers" and "Put Your Head On My 
Shoulder." The Anka story is indeed an amazing 
one and this set captures it to a tee. 
IT'LL SHINE WHEN IT SHINES - The Ozark 
Mountain Daredevils - Producers: Glyn Johns, 
David Anderle - A&M SP -3654 
If you want to go to heaven you'd better not 
pass up this dynamic new Ozark Mt. Daredevil LP 
-it's really too good to miss. The amiable coun- 
try rockers have put some fine sounds together 
here and each cut reflects the growing maturity 
which has distinguished it on its climb to the top. 
Featured on this disk are some excellent tunes, 
particularly "You Made It Right," "Tidal Wave," 
"It Couldn't Be Better" and the stunning title 
track, a tune for everyone. 
THE MARK OF THE BEAST - Willie Hutch - 
Producer: Willie Hutch - Motown M6 -815S1 
The sartorial Mr. Hutch once again demon- 
strates his ability to get down and put it where it's 
at with this bold new LP, a collection of soulful 
funk that undeniably elevates him to the top of 
the genre. His production and arrangements on 
each tune lend definitive character to his 
material and makes his unique stamp unmistaka- 
ble. We particularly dig "Get Ready For The Get 
Down," "Don't You Let Nobody Tell You How To 
Do Your Thing" and "Life's No Fun Living In The 
Ghetto." 
WHILE YOU'RE DOWN THERE - Stray Dog - 
Producers: Austin Godsey. Stray Dog - Man- 
ticore MA6-501 S1 
Now distributed through Motown, Manticore's 
roster of artists is starting to live up to the poten- 
tial they displayed on their initial efforts. Stray 
Dog is an excellent case in point. The group has 
expanded from a trio into a powerhouse quintet 
with diverse roots that come together with the 
force of a tidal wave on this disk. Highlighted by 
such cuts as "Calamity Jane," "Junkyard Angel," 
"Bits & Pieces," "Words To Say Goodbye" and 
"Worldwinds," the LP sparkles with inescapable 
energy. 
pop picks 
Brian Auger's Oblivion Express 
FOR YOU - Eddie Kendricks - Producers: 
Frank Wilson, Leonard Caston - Tamla T6 -335S1 
That "Son of Sagittarius," Mr. "Boogie Down" 
himself, is truckin' again on his new Tamla LP, 
but the pace has mellowed and the emphasis is 
decidedly on Kendricks' ability to lay down some 
of the most soulful love ballads ever recorded. 
Splendid production and tactful arrangements 
on each of the eight cuts (including Jim Croce's 
"Time In A Bottle") enhance the message Eddie 
is carrying and nowhere is this more apparent 
than on "Shoeshine Boy." We also dig "Let 
Yourself Go" and "Please Don't Go Away." 
THE LAMB LIES DOWN ON BROADWAY - 
Genesis - Atco SD2-401 
Among the leaders of the avant garde move- 
ment in rock, Genesis definitely has itself a 
blockbuster of an LP in this dynamic two record 
set which once again features the far-reaching 
lyrics and musical sophistication that has pro- 
pelled the band into prominence, a position they 
well deserve. Highlighting this twin record are 
some marvelous pieces of music, including 
"Broadway Melody of 1974," "Counting Out 
Time," "The Supernatural Anaesthetist," "Riding 
The Scree" and "Silent Sorrow In Empty Boats." 
Great word pictures again. 
ME 'N ROCK 'N ROLL ARE HERE TO STAY - 
David Ruffin - Producer: Norman Whitfield - 
Motown M6 -818S1 
The fabulous David Ruffin, truly one of the 
finest soul singers in the history of the genre 
comes forth with an exciting new Motown LP that 
features his vocal ability applied to a strong col- 
lection of tunes. "I Saw You When You Met Her" 
is typical of the "tell it like it is" type of tune he 
delivers with such authority. Other exceptional 
tracks from this well conceived LP are "Smiling 
Faces Sometimes," "Superstar (Remember How 
You Got Where You Are)," "I Just Want To 
Celebrate" and the fine title track. 
I JUST WANT TO SING WITH MY FRIENDS - 
Persuasions - Producer: Jeff Barry - A&M SP 
3656 
The group that developed a capella to its 
highest state in the 70's combines that great 
form with some tremendous music on their latest 
A&M LP. The Persuasions are undoubtedly the 
number one a capella group, but their talents 
aren't restricted to that purest music alone. On 
this disk they get down and party with abandon 
on such cuts as "I'm A Hog For You Baby," 
"Somewhere To Lay My Head" and the fantastic 
title track. Make no mistake, this is a super 
group. 
COOK - P.F.M. - P.F.M. - Producers: Claudio 
Fabi, P.F.M. - Manticore MA6-502S1 
Italy's top group and another Manticore suc- 
cess story in the making leaps out at you with this 
bold new LP, a disk loaded with the high energy 
that has made PFM one of the most popular acts 
on the concert circuit. The raw gutsy vocals and 
lead guitar riffs harken back the experimental 
stages of Cream and the Yardbirds and each cut 
emphasizes that PFM is definitely a group of the 
future. Listen to "Four Holes In The Ground" and 
"Mr. Nine Till Five" and you'll get the picture. 
UVE OBLIVION VOL. 1 - Brian Auger's Oblivion 
Express - Producer: Brian Auger - RCA 
CPL1-0645 
Recorded live at Hollywood's Whiskey A Go 
Go, this LP captures the live essence of Brian 
Auger's Oblivion Express to a tee. The energy, 
creativity and innovation that have been so much 
a part of the group are all present in various 
moods and textures, each of which is entirely 
convincing and thoroughly professional down to 
the last detail. We like in particular "Beginning 
Again," "Bumpin' On Sunset" and "Truth," but 
the fourth cut "Don't Look Away" is a gem also. A 
fine LP.

HERE'S JOHNNY - MAGIC MOMENTS FROM 
THE TONIGHT SHOW - Various Artists - 
Producers: Joyce Biawitz, Bernard Fox - 
Casablanca SPNB 1296 
A fantastic two record set, including a special 
poster, this LP offers some of the best music and 
comedy ever to be released in one package. 
Commemorating the Johnny Carson success 
story and the many stars who have emerged after 
appearing on his NBC-TV nightly talk show the 
set features appearances by Groucho Marx, Ike 
& Tina Turner. Bette Midler, Lenny Bruce, Pearl 
Bailey, Sammy Davis, Aretha Franklin, The 
Smothers Brothers and the unforgettable Art 
Fern (Art Fern?). 
THE TURTLES' GREATEST HITS - The Turtles - 
Sire SASH - 3703-2 
Subtitled "Hoppy Together Again," this 
fabulous Turtles' two record deluxe set is a 
refreshing blast from our romantic past and 
features one of the sixties' most popular groups 
doing a number of chart hits they offered con- 
secutively over the span of several years. The 
Flo & Eddie duo, so popular today, emanated 
from the Turtles and their influence is laced 
heavily throughout the hits "It Ain't Me Babe," 
"Elenore," "Happy Together" and "Can I Get To 
Know You Better." 
SATIN DOLL - Bobbi Humphrey - Producers: 
Larry Mizell, Chuck Davis - Blue Note BN- 
LA344-G 
The superb talent of Bobbi Humphrey breaks 
through on her new LP as never before with the 
lady singing and playing flute with the dexterity 
achieved only by true virtuosos. Accompanied 
by a cast of skillful and innovative backup musi- 
cians, Bobbi casts her spell on such tracks as 
"New York Times," "Ladies Day." "You Are The 
Sunshine Of My Life," "My Little Girl" and "San 
Francisco Lights." On each cut the lady proves 
that she's a genuine genius. 
I CAN HELP - Billy Swan - Producers: Chip 
Young, Billy Swan - Monument KZ 33279 
The title track of Billy's bright new LP is #1 on 
this week's CASH BOX charts and it's certainly 
easy to see why. Not only is the single top 
drawer, but the entire collection of songs is im- 
peccably tailored to fit a variety of tastes. Swan's 
vocals are emotional where necessary and to the 
point when the material calls for it ("Don't Be 
Cruel," a slow version that provides an interest- 
ing counterpart to Elvis' version). We like "Lover 
Please" and "Queen of My Heart" a lot. 
THE BEST OF TYMES - The Tymes - Abcko 
AA4228 
The Tymes, currently on the charts with "You 
Little Trustmaker" now find themselves the sub- 
ject of a 'tyme'-ly LP featuring some of their 
finest hits of the sixties. Highlighting this 
package are the monster smashes "So Much In 
Love," "Wonderful Wonderful," "Chances Are," 
"Twelfth Of Never" and "Goodnight My Love." 
The impeccable harmonies the group made 
famous are here in abundance and keep the 
smooth tempo rippling with musical excitement. 
ROCK'N RHODES CHRISTMAS - The Rhodes 
Kids - Producers: Danny Janssen, Bobby Hart 
- GRC GA10011 
With less than a month till old St. Nick attempts 
to slide his rotund body down a million chimneys 
at once, the Rhodes Kids have gotten the jump 
on the Yuletide season with a bright album 
geared to the holiday season and the emotional 
attachments so many share for this time of the 
year. Included in this bright disk are "Winter 
Wonderland," "Joy To The World," "Christmas 
Medley," "Christmas All Year Through" and 
"Santa Loves Rock 'n Roll Music." So do the 
Rhodes Kids.

THE BITTER END YEARS - Various Artists - 
Roxbury RLX 300 
A spectacular three record set, this ROXBURY 
PACKAGE CAPSULIZES THE HISTORY OF 
ONE OF New York's most famous night spots, 
the Bitter End. The three records each deal with 
different times and moods; "Early Times," featur- 
ing Theodore Bikel, Everly Bros., Peter, Paul & 
Mary and Judy Collins; "Comedy Teams" includ- 
ing Woody Allen. George Carlin, David Frye, 
Robert Klein, David Steinberg and Lily Tomlin 
and; "Rock Years" with John Denver, lsley Bros., 
Curtis Mayfield, Van Morrison and Bette Midler. 
An incredible package. 
ANDY KIM'S GREATEST HITS - Andy Kim - 
ABC/Dunhill DSPD-50193 
With Andy's single "Rock Me Gently" having 
just come off a number one chart spot, 
ABC/Dunhill has taken the occasion to release a 
greatest hits LP featuring the artist doing a 
number of rock standards from "Be My Baby" 
and "Baby, 
I Love You" to "So Good Together" 
and "A Friend In The City." Throughout the col- 
lection, Andy's vocals are the soul and substance 
that provides listener motivation in terms of 
positive response. This LP definitely lends 
credence to his claim to stardom. 
ALBERT HAMMOND - Albert Hammond - 
Producers: A. Hammond, Roy Halee - Mums KZ 
32834 
It never rains in Southern California and for 
Albert Hammond this new Mums LP will keep 
the rain away from his door for a long long time. 
Featuring his new single, "We're Running Out." 
Hammond's new disk is a combination of smooth 
melodies and introspective lyrics that blend 
together into a contiguous harmony -a musical 
tapestry made of the finest cloth. Tight arrange- 
ment and precision dynamics hold the excellent 
songs together and the package comes off with 
total professionalism. 
WHITE HORSE - Michael Omartian - Producer: 
Michael Omartian - ABC/Dunhill DSD-50185 
THE RENOWNED PRODUCER WHO ONCE 
WAS A MEMBER OF THE Loggins and Messina 
band as a pianist now ventures forth with an ex- 
traordinary LP that proves that you never know 
just how many talents as artist has till he shows 
them to you. Omartian on this LP not only dis- 
plays his poise and professionalism as a pro- 
ducer, but also as an artist on such tracks as "Fat 
City," "The Rest Is Up To You," "Take Me Down" 
and "Add Up The Wonders." A man of diverse 
talents, Omartian opens up new worlds with this 
LP. 
AIN'T GONNA PLAY NO SECOND FIDDLE - 
Dana Gillespie - Producers: Dana Gillespie. 
John Porter - RCA CPL1-0682 
The vivacious and exciting Dana Gillespie's 
second LP for MainMan and RCA is as scintillat- 
ing as the first, but more titillating. Dana does her 
level best to project sexy independence and 
comes across convincingly with her 
performances. The LP sparkles with first person 
reality and some very strong musical tracks. Our 
particular favorites are "Get My Rocks Off," 
"Wanderlust," "Pack Your Bags" and the "No 
Holds Barred" title track. 
WINNIE THE POO AND TIGGER TOO - Sebastian 
Cabot, Sterling Holloway, Paul Winchell - Dis- 
neyland 3813 
A fantastic children's package for the 
Christmas season or for any season, this Dis- 
neyland package comes complete with a full col- 
or illustrated book to go with the record, a 
magnificent rendering of Disney-esque fairy tale 
told by Sebastian Cabot (narrator). Sterling 
Holloway (Winnie The Pool) and Paul Winchell 
(Tigger). The story is pure fun and the 
performances splendid so all you kids from 2 to 
82 go get it.

cash box FMB news report 
r&b ingredients 
Capitol recording artists Tavares have been slated to perform at the MGM Grand 
Hotel in Las Vegas for a month long appearance beginning Nov. 27. The Tavares 
brothers have enjoyed increasing popularity ever since they signed with Capitol 
Records in 1973. Their latest LP "Hard Core Poetry" and their single "She's Gone" 
have both done well in the R&B charts (the single is #3 with a bullet) and everyone is 
looking forward to their Las Vegas opening. ... L.T.D., whose new album "Gittin' 
Down" was just released, are planning a tour in which they will use ancient African in- 
struments from Zaire. The instruments, like the kuba harp which is a type of lute 
played with a bow, will add an exotic dash to this eleven man funk band. Some of the 
instruments are over 500 years old.... Steve Metz and Alan Klein have set up an 
Australian tour for Avco artists Limmie & Family Cookin' from Dec. 8 to Jan. 4 now that 
their record, "A Walkin' Miracle" is a hit down under.... Philly Groove recording 
artists Finishing Touch have released their new single "Your Love Has A Spell On 
Me." The trio of male singers have "Second Best (Is Never Enough)" on the flip side 
and with their rhythm section, The Last Word, have been touring across the country. 
... Based on the strength of her Epic Records album "Perfect Angel," Chess/Janus 
Records has re-released an old Minnie Riperton LP called "Come To My Garden," 
which has also gone on the charts. "Garden" was first distributed four years ago. Min- 
nie's new Epic single "Seeing You This Way" was also just released.... Etta James 
was special guest artist on two recent sold -out Van Morrison concerts at the Anaheim 
Convention Center and at the Sacramento Memorial Auditorium.... Philly Soulville 
Records has released the Sound Experience's latest single, "Your Love Belongs To 
Me." The tune was taken from the group's current LP "Don't Fight The Feeling." The 
Sound Experience personnel includes Gregory Holmes, tenor sax; Reginald Wright, 
lead trumpet; Rodney Parks, drums; James Lindsey, alto sax; Melvin Miles, Jr.,

Rustic Records 
Signs Garrett 
HOLLYWOOD - Rustic Records, the in- 
dependently -owned label of The 
Checkmates Ltd., has signed Vernon 
Garrett to an exclusive recording con- 
tract, announced Neal Ames, vice- 
president and general manager of 
Rustic. 
Garrett has achieved major promi- 
nence with his recordings of "Lonely, 
Lonely Night," "Without You," and 
"Angel Doll," and has also produced a 
number of records for various indepen- 
dent record companies around the coun- 
try. 
Rustic also signed Bill McCloud, 
formerly of MCA Records, to produce 
Garrett's recordings through Los 
Angeles West Production Company. 
Ames stated that "with the proven 
talents of Garrett and McCloud, plus a 
fresh approach to promotion, Rustic an- 
ticipates strong consumer recognition of 
the initial product which is scheduled for 
release in early 1975." 
Pictured above to congratulate Garrett 
are (from left): Bobby Stevens, president 
of the label and manager of The 
Checkmates Ltd.; Bill McCloud; and Neal 
Ames.

O'Neal Twins Day 
HOLLYWOOD - The O'Neal Twins. 
Shelter Records premier Gospel artists 
celebrated their twenty-fifth anniversary 
of performing together with a concert at 
the Kiel Auditorium (St. Louis) Sunday 
Nov. 3. Headlining the show along with 
the O'Neal Twins were The Staple 
Singers and Reverend James Cleveland. 
Other notable gospel groups were the 
Brooklyn All Stars, Reverend Maceo 
Woods and the Interfaith Choir. 
In addition to the concert, Mayor John 
Poelker honored the Twins for their 
many years of faithful service to the St. 
Louis community by proclaiming Sunday 
O'Neal Twins Day. 
Shelter Records under the direction of 
Leon Russell and Patrick Henderson 
taped the concert with the assistance of 
Fedco (well known for its fine job on 
the "Mad Dogs and Englishmen" LP). 
The Twins first Shelter album just re- 
cently released was produced by Leon 
Russell and Patrick Henderson and de- 
buted on the Gospel charts at number 
thirty-one. 
Jazz Presented 
On Cable TV 
NEW YORK - An advanced concept in 
musical entertainment has started on 
Sterling Manhattan cable television. 
Every Monday night at 11:30, on public 
access channel D, the Experimental 
Television Coop is presenting "live" jazz 
and contemporary musicans, performing 
in a relaxed, intimate format that 
stimulates creativity on a level not pos- 
sible on commercial television. The 
name of the show is "Jamming." 
Frank Watkins is the producer/director 
of the show and Mike Garr acts as asst. 
producer.

Motown Marketing And Creative

HOLLYWOOD - Motown Records held 
a marketing and creative services meet- 
ing for all Motown regional promotion 
and regional sales managers last week at 
the Holiday Inn in Westwood. The pro- 
motion and sales managers were 
brought to town for the two day session 
to discuss the November release. 
The first day of the meetings, directed 
by Tom Noonan, acting director of 
marketing, was devoted to promotion, 
sales, distribution and the formation of 
the plans, contests and assignments to 
work this product. The regional 
managers were told how all were to 
coordinate their efforts with Motown's 
distributors, the tours of the artists, and 
with radio stations. 
Ewart Abner, president of Motown 
Records, made a special presentation 
dealing with each person's 
responsibilities and discussing Motown's 
future and their part in that future. 
Herb Belkin, vice president of creative 
operations, presided over the second 
day's meetings. These meetings outlined 
support plans of the new product dealing 
with advertising, merchandising, publici- 
ty, graphics, artists relations and the in- 
troduction of the new releases. 
Belkin presented a new image in an- 
nouncing the recent acquisition of dis- 
tribution rights for Manticore Records 
and introducing the new Melodyland 
label, Motown's C&W wing, thereby 
broadening the base and giving the corn- 
pany greater diversification in terms of 
artists, product and potential.

Oscar Peterson, the Canadian jazz pianist, angrily cancelled a concert tour of the 
Soviet Union and left for Helsinki. Peterson was piqued by the treatment received 
from Soviet officials. He left Moscow right before he was to perform at the first of 4 
sold out concerts.... Dom Um Romao will be leaving Weather Report at the end of 
the year. He plans to return to Brazil and put together a new group, called "Hot- 
mospheres." The act will be composed on Brazilian musicians. Um Romao has just 
finished his second album for Muse. Joe Beck, Dom Salvador and Guillermo Franco 
will appear on it. Weather Report has just finished a major tour. They are presently in 
Calif. preparing their 5th album. The group plans to add a female vocalist.... Watch 
for a major contemporary jazz release on Arista Records via the distribution arrange- 
ment of an important European catalogue. Some of the records are by Cecil Taylor, 
Randy Weston, Gato Barbieri and Ornette Coleman. ... The N.Y. Jazz Museum re- 
cently opened an exhibit entitled "Count Basie And His Bands." Membership in the 
museum is also available. Members receive an engraved membership card, a free LP, 
discounts on purchases at The Jazz Store, free admission to the annual Christmas 
party, discounts on special events, and free classified advertising in "Hot Notes" the 
jazz newsletter. Active membership costs $15 per year. There are special rates for 
students. Dues are payable on a calendar -year basis.... Leroy Jenkins will hold a 
Workshop at Columbia beginning on Jan. 27 at 7:30 p.m. It will take place at The 
McMillon Theatre on the Columbia campus.... ESP disk has revitalized its record's 
graphics. Similar themes will be represented, but the albums will have a new form. 
Spencer Drate will head -up the project's avant-garde graphics dept.... A 12 minute 
free color film on the Blackbyrds is available from Fantasy's west coast office. The 
movie shows the group attending classes at Howard University, in performance and 
in the studio.... Denmark Records held its 20th anniversary party last week. Among 
the talent performing at the gala was Big Joe Williams, Sleepy John Estes, and Ham - 
mie Nixon. Most of the major Chicago bluesmen were in attendance.... Donald Byrd 
and the Blackbyrds have just finished scoring a movie entitled "Hit The Open Man." 
... "Billy Taylor Lecture Series" started at Howard Univ. last month. Taylor will lec- 
ture on many aspects of jazz. The series will be bi -monthly.

YESTERDAYS - Gato Barbieri - Flying Dutch- 
man - 0698 
The first side is an interesting combination of 
Kern and Harbach's standard, "Yesterdays," and 
the Trane's "A John Coltrane Blues." On the 
former, the first few bars of the intro remind one 
of Pharoah, yet, the Latin rhythms are clearly 
Barbieri's. Gato always rhythmically enlivens the 
somewhat sterile bossa nova percussion line. 
See the first chorus here. 8 -bars of congas open 
"The Blues." The instruments are introduced in- 
dividually (note Paul Metzke's guitar work). After 
Gato announces the head, his choruses blend 
the Trane's mysticism with his own musical 
anarchism (see the twisted notes, weak -beat syn- 
copations, and multi -octave excursions). 
SINGERELLA - Gary Bartz - Prestige - 
P-10083 
The fairy tale is one of "rats, roaches, and 
melon coaches." "St. Felix St." epitomizes the 
album's mood. At times, the music, like ghetto 
life, labors under the logic of a dominant force. 
Yet the human, and the humor involved in the in- 
visible world is also present. Bartz' sop sax 
chorus portrays all the tension lurking below the 
apathy of the depraved existence. The vocals are 
matter-of-fact statements, or better, exhorta- 
tions, that can lay bare frustration and ac- 
complishment in a single phrase (see 
"Singerella" and "Nation Time"). 
FRESH FEATHERS - John Klemmer - Impulse 
ABCD-836 
John Klemmer's 9th album. The record blends 
a rock beat with jazz improvisations. The first 
side, however, seems to revolve around Klem- 
mer's changes of the melody lines within a 
tightened 4/4 structure. He adds certain little 
rhythmic twists to keep the tracks interesting. On 
"Fresh Feather's" second chorus, Klemmer ac- 
cents the weak beat and ties notes across 
measures, breaking the restrictions of the bar 
line. The second side is more loosely structured 
and open-ended. Note "Stinger," with a modal 
intro which nicely blends into the scalar theme. 
JOE & ZOOT - Joe Venuti and Zoot Sims - 
Chiaroscuro CR 128 
A meeting of two masters. The album's in- 
teresting sound arises from the empathetic com- 
bination of two radically different instruments. 
Because the two musicians are sensitive to the 
different qualities of the sax and the violin, the 
music works and assumes an airy quality. "Some- 
day, Sweetheart," has counterpointed duets 
which are devoid of excess ornamentation -a 
common fault of swing - and which still 
manages a few rhythmic surprises. On "C Jam 
Blues," note the woven melody lines which 
create a spatial wonder reminiscent of the Duke 
himself. 
POUM - Fischer, Robinson, Whitecage, Cook, 
Pavonex - Composers Collective 721 
The Composers Collective was formed in 1972 
in order to produce music that is not commercial- 
ly available. The music demands that the listener 
put aside all notions regarding normal musical 
structure, that he try to listen to the music from a 
perspective similar to that of the musicians who 
composed the pieces. That perspective is 
enlightened, indeed. "Sinfonia" is quite abstract 
and proceeds over spatial planes as well as over 
time. Yet it also, interestingly, seems to double 
back upon itself. The "Apollo" series is 
thematically structured around the first moon 
landing. 
THE JAZZ PIANO OF JOHN COATES, JR. - John 
Coates, Jr. - Omnisound N 1004 
The second production of Omnisound, Inc. 
and the first album for Coates. Note the two 
resolutions in "Love Is Enough." After the first, 
Kay on bass and Davis on drums join in accom- 
paniment. The piece is sharpened by interesting 
dischords, and arpeggio runs which confront the 
piece's time signature. Immediately preceeding 
the coda is a fine example of Coates contrapuntal 
harmonic technique. After a modal opening on 
"Yesterday," Coates creatively explodes the 
tunes harmonic and rhythmic structure.

---- p31
JAZZ ARTIST OF THE MONTH - 
Return to Forever 
Jazz musicians have always had to grapple with the problem of properly mixing 
musical virtuosity and commerciality. One band which has successfully skirted the 
fine line between creative obscurity and the big sell-out is Return to Forever. The 
members of the group have paid their dues with many of jazz's most progressive acts. 
Chick Corea, Forever's leader, for example, has played with Miles Davis on the 
watershed album, "Bitches Brew." Circle, co -led by Corea, Anthony Braxton, Dave 
Holland, and Barry Altschul, has cut some of the finest abstract, experimental tracks 
in recent years. However, as Corea says, Return to Forever's aim is "to bring good 
music to a lot of people. In the process of developing as a band, we changed from be- 
ing art -for -arts sake musicians into musicians who want to contact and communicate 
with audiences." The music of Return to Forever does not talk down to the audience, 
nor does it lose them in technicalities and subtleties known only to the professional 
musician and critic. The success of the group's latest tour and the sales on the 
Polydor album "Where Have I Known You Before?" seems to indicate that the band's 
aim has been achieved. 
Return to Forever is composed of Chick Corea on keyboards, Stanley Clarke on 
bass, Lennie White on drums, and Al DiMeola on guitar. Though the musicians are 
young - Corea is the oldest at 33, while Clarke and DiMeola are in their early 20's - 
they have already garnered many awards. "Downbeats" 1973 International Critic's 
poll named Corea "Composer of the Year," and Clarke the top bassist (Clarke has also 
received the 1974 award). The 1974 Jazz Forum Poll named Corea "Jazz Musician of 
the World." Melody Maker sighted the group's second LP "Hymm of the 7th Galaxy" 
as the #2 album of the year. 
The music is a unique combination of the talents of four musicians, each of whom is 
treated as a distinct musical individual. Their three Polydor albums, "Light As A 
Feather," "Hymn," and "Where Have 
I Known You Before?" are products of all the 
member's abilities; no musician takes a secondary role. Clarke said, "I'm allowed to be 
the way I want to be, the way 
I am. Everyone allows everyone else beingness, the 
space to be himself and to grow." White added "We communicate our affinity for each 
other visually and the people can see that too. As we grow together as a band, the 
power is more evenly spaced. DiMeola stated, "This band communicates more than 
the other bands I've played in. Nobody is on an ego-trip, which is a refreshing 
change." 
Electronic and rhythmic, the band's tunes encourage intellectual listening and 
dancing at the same time. Neither moment is sacrificed at the expense of the other. 
"Our music," Corea reflected, "is more composed now and the rhythm is stabler and 
the beat more firmly stated. We want people to have fun with our music, to dance to it 
and to sing it. The most challenging part now is to retain our musical integrity while in- 
volving people and bringing them into rapport with us. Everybody in the band is com- 
posing and everybody is involved in constantly re-evaluating our goals, so that the 
music is always fresh." 
The band's name, which has confused many listeners, is a metaphysical oxymoron. 
It does, however, yield an insight into the character of the group. "Return to Forever" 
conjures a sense of wholeness, in which totality, once lost, has been regained. Corea, 
commenting on the composition, "Where Have I Known You Before?" explained, "it 
speaks very easily, almost naively about the fact that you're a spiritual being in the un- 
iverse and have lived many lifetimes. The truth of that can be seen in the people's 
positive reactions." 
"If you can continue that feeling of wholeness with good musicianship," Corea con- 
cluded, "then you have a fine way of revealing moments of truth." 
The band has successfully bridged the precarious gap between wide popularity 
and minute professional interest. The group's future will only be a return to forever.

all that's jazz 
picks of the week 
THE SAXOPHONE - Various Artists - Impulse 
- ASH - 9253-3 
THE BASS - Various Artists - Impulse - ASH 
- 9284-3 
THE DRUMS - Various Artists - Impulse - ASH 
- 9272-3 
Steve Backer and Ed Michel have put together 
a series of specially priced and lavishly boxed tri- 
ple albums structured around the jazz develop- 
ment of the drum, the bass, and the saxophone. 
While there obviously will never be a definitive 
study of any instrument, these packages are the 
best to date. Each album comes with extensive 
liner notes explaining the tracks and the musi- 
cians who play on them. Robert Palmer, a jazz 
writer, has also spiced the critical writings with a 
discussion of the various instruments 
morphology. The bass music covers Duke ElI- 
ington's band, Pharoah Sanders' group and ever- 
yone in between. In many ways, the highlight of 
the album is "II BS," featuring Charlie Mingus. In 
addition to Mingus' opening, catch the work of 
Jaki Byard and Eric Dolphy. Side Three of "The 
Saxophone" is a veritable compendium of the 
most progressive reed men of the past 30 years. 
Lester Young, Eric Dolphy (with Booker Little), 
and Ornette Coleman (with the Liberation 
Orchestra) are highlighted on this magnificent 
side. If you can't imagine Creed Taylor produc- 
ing Cecil Taylor, check out side five of "The 
Drums." Sunny Murray's polyrhythmic work on 
"Pots" emerges from the traditional secondary 
position to share the spotlight, even though he 
does not solo. 
SATAN - Sonny Stitt - Cadet - CA 50060 
Stitt offers a combination of Roland Hanna's 
compositions, the Coffin -King pop standard, 
"Will You Love Me Tomorrow?," and "It Might As 
Well Be Spring." On "Will You," Stitt almost does 
what always should have been done to the piece. 
Two choruses of approximately 16 bars are 
rhythmically spiced with interesting uses of rests 
and weak -beat syncopations. Unfortunately, the 
remainder of his solos are merely paraphrases. 
On "Anyòne," Hanna's 12 -bar intro on acoustic 
piano leads into a heavily rhythmic ostinato an- 
nounced by the horns. Stitt's solos offer an in- 
sight into the creative possibilities still present in 
techniques developed in the '40's. 
GET UP WITH IT - Miles Davis - Col. X 698 
Miles Davis has put together his most exciting 
and creative LP since "Jack Johnson." The disk 
length demands attentive listening, yet the en- 
joyment is well worth the effort. The album was 
made "For Duke." Davis developed the ideas for 
a tribute to Ellington while attending the funeral 
of the orchestral master. Side 1 is the monumen- 
tal "He Loved Him Madly." The piece sounds as 
if the Duke himself was in the control room. 
Davis orchestrates several freely woven layers of 
music. The echoplex helps create the sensation 
of an entire instrumental section. The piece 
moves in time while it expands vertically in 
space. 
IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST - Gary Burton and 
Mike Gibbs - Polydor PD 6503 
Mike Gibbs is a Rhodesian trombonist and 
pianist who conducts the large orchestra. His 
"Start of Something Similar," begins with Al 
Zavod and then Gary Burton announcing the 
3 -bar rhythmic motif. The entire orchestra is then 
added as the section of horns announce the 
composition's theme. Burton's percussive solo is 
nicely sparked by legato -like arpeggios. Also, 
note Mike Brecker's solo. The title track has 
several ostinado statements by the entire or- 
chestra and uniquely contrasts several rockish 
sections with somewhat more tranquil episodes 
in a rondo of excitement and calm. 
MUSIQUE DU BOIS - Phil Woods - Muse 5037 
Woods' first record date as a leader since his 
return from Europe after a 5 -year stay on the 
continent. "Nefertit" is slow, bluesy, and gutsy. 
Compare Woods' interpretation with Circle's ren- 
dition. Note Woods' slap-tongueing on the tag. 
"The Last Page" has a nice ballad -like intro. It 
mixes 5/4 and 4/4 times. The latter sections are 
extremely mellow, the former picks up the pace. 
Check Richard Davis' backing and solo here. 
Joining Woods on alto and Davis on bass are Jaki 
Byard on acoustic piano and Alan Dawson on the 
drums.

LOS ANGELES - The Jackson Five, 
Motown recording artists who recently 
closed a headline engagement at the 
MGM Grand Hotel in Las Vegas, have 
cancelled all personal appearances for 
the month of Jan. and will spend the time 
recording at MoWest studios. 
According to a group spokesman, "the 
group will not only be recording a new 
group album, but will concentrate on 
new individual albums for members of 
the group. 
"Since they are already contractually 
committed for appearances in Las Vegas, 
Lake Tahoe, three foreign tours, aside 
from their regular theatre -in -the -round 
appearances and concerts, we decided 
to block out some time for recording 
prior to hitting the road again." 
SIGNED, SOULED AND DELIVERED - 
Shown at the re-signing of Blue Note 
artist Horace Silver are (from left, stand- 
ing) Al Teller, president of United Artists 
Records, which distributes Blue Note; 
George Butler, general manager of Blue 
Note; and Sara Boyers of United Artists' 
legal department; the center of their at- 
tention is Silver himself, shown smiling 
at the camera after signing his contract. 
The innovative musician, long known as 
the father of the "soul school" of jazz, is 
scheduled to release a new Blue Note 
album early next year.

picks of the week 
MOVIN' DAY - Grady Tate - Janus JXS 7010 
Grady Tate's first album as a lead vocalist. Tate 
has a mellow timbre and an extremely attractive 
tone. He can handle a soulful ballad as well as an 
uptempo pop tune. The selection of material ex- 
ploits his enormous musical knowledge. The in- 
strumental backing swings within the tight vocal 
structure. Check Ron Carter's bass on Van Mor- 
rison's "Moondance." On the second verse, his 
triplet and dotted 16th groups energize the 
vocals. "Sitting in Limbo" is a blues number, 
highlighted by Elliot Randall's guitar work. Also 
appearing on the album are Joe Farrell, Joe 
Newman, and Jimmy Johnson. 
THE WORLD OF SWING - Various Artists - Col 
X698 
This double LP fills in many gaps in previously 
released swing collections. Many of the cuts are 
obscure; some, in fact, have never been issued 
before. The tracks are arranged chronologically 
and show the developments in the band struc- 
ture. Stanley Dance, the author of "The Worlds 
of Swing," provides excellent liner notes. Chick 
Webb's "Stompin' At The Savoy," highlights the 
drummer and Sandy Williams on trombone. Ell- 
ington and Basie's Orchestras are heard 
together on "One More Once." The cut features 
the two band's sax sections. Checkout Paul 
Gonzalves' coda. 
LOVE IS IN US ALL - Pharoah Sanders - Im- 
pulse - ASD 9200 
The album has two extended cuts. The first is 
entitled "Love is in Us All," while the second side 
is an ode "To John." The title track is very 
rhythmic and, as expected, is replete with 
percussion instruments. The two -bar ostinado is 
developed in two sections. In the first, the 
melody is sung, while the polyrhythms are 
woven about the lyrics. There is an interesting 
chordal break by the piano before the first sec- 
tion closes. The tempo is slowed down in the 
second section, which consists of Sander's alto 
work counterpointed with the piano. 
STORIES TO TELL - Flora Purim - Milestone - 
M-9058 
Flora Purim, "downbeat's" top female vocalist 
of 1974, has released her second album. The ti- 
tle track, composed by Miroslav Vitous and 
Purim, includes titles and phrases from Neville 
Potter's pieces for the first Return to Forever. 
Check out Vitous' Moog work here. Purim has 
composed lyrics for McCoy Tyner's "Search for 
Piece." Her voice on the piece is sensuous and 
haunting; it readily evokes the sentiments of the 
song. George Duke's superb accompaniment on 
acoustic piano creatively utilizes Tyner's pen- 
tatonic chord structure. 
FACING YOU - Keith Jarrett - ECM 1017 ST 
Keith Jarrett again performs solo piano. 
Though the LP was released in Europe in 1972, it 
is now readily available through Polydor in the 
States. The record is more consistent than the 
"Solo Concerts" triple LP, and has none of the 
"Concert" LPs' sterile, "technique -for -technique - 
sake" lapses. Jarrett's work includes both strong 
chordal rhythms and light legato arpeggios. "In 
Front" steps right out and brightly dances over 
the heavy bass part. "My Lady; My Child" is a soft 
and striking ode. The chord progression here is 
quite interesting. 
ALONE TOGETHER - Joseph Jarman and An- 
thony Braxton - Delmark DS -428 
The record features Joseph Jarman of the Art 
Ensemble of Chicago and Anthony Braxton, a 
one-time member of Circle and an outstanding 
composer. Both are extremely talented reedists. 
The compositions on side 1 are Braxton's, while 
the second side is devoted to Jarman's work. 
The title track begins with the two saxes in un- 
ison. Though they play together, the single voice 
sounds isolated and alone. Yet, the voice divides 
and Jarman and Braxton creatively play against 
each other. "CK7 (GN)" is non -structured, 
polyrhythmic, and extremely abstract. The piece 
tries to clarify the relationship between pure 
sound and music.

all that's jazz 
George Benson - Bad Is Good 
As a result of the current fascination with jazz 
rock fusionists such as Larry 
Coryell, Al DiMeola, John McLaughlin and John Abercrombie, interest has carried 
over to several guitarists who adopt a somewhat purer stance. People are listening to 
Jim Hall. Kenny Burrell, Pat Martino and Joe Pass again, and George Benson, who 
many consider the most likely to inherit the late Wes Montgomery's patriarchal 
crown, is getting booked into rock clubs like the Bottom Line in addition to jazz 
strongholds like the Half Note. 
With Benson's new album, "Bad Benson" on CTI. he shows considerable advance- 
ments over earlier recordings which tended to reflect a cool. unobtrusive perfection 
about his playing. There was never any question about his technical abilities. but he 
never seemed to command much attention from the listener. With his last album. 
"Body Talk." things began to loosen up. On "Bad Benson," his tenth album, he has 
begun to express something of himself in his playing with a greater reliance on 
natural instinct and his r&b background. "This one is a new experience for me." he 
says. "I've played with different musicians of different calibres in different idioms but 
on this record I lean more toward my level of harmony." 
Benson's first recording was. ironically enough, made when he was part of a singing 
group in 1953. The record took the shortcut to obscurity outside of his home town of 
Pittsburgh. so he took up the guitar. He played with a couple of r&b groups until his 
father coaxed him into auditioning for jazzman Jack McDuff who was playing an 
engagement just outside of Pittsburgh. "McDuff's band was swinging harder than 
anyone else I had ever heard before. I was saying that if there was anybody I would 
like to play with, it would be him." 
Benson recalls that he could hardly play at the time. but six months later, he found 
himself in the group. "I managed to hide the fact that I didn't know how to solo until 
I 
embarassed myself one night. so he put me on notice - 
I was on notice with McDuff 
for three years. The thing that made the group was that I was in the middle playing r&b 
and borrowing from jazz at the same time. McDuff didn't like it. but it was only through 
him telling me that it wouldn't work that gave me the urge to keep trying." 
Benson led his first group in 1965 but found himself caught in the rock and roll 
groundswell which relegated him to playing disco -type clubs - often sandwiched 
between gyrating go-go girls in cages. Since then. Benson has had numerous groups 
of his own design, slowly moving away from r&b and toward a full -tilt jazz sound in the 
process. 
A recent interest in production techniques has already resulted in an album 
Benson produced for his keyboardman, Ronnie Foster. "Rock groups generally make 
better albums than jazz groups because they enjoy more freedom." he maintains. 
"Obviously. if you can go into the studio with whomever you have working for you at 
the time, you will sound more together. Changing the whole structure of the group or 
playing with guys you don't even know can't help but make yourfeel uncomfortable. 
The only jazz musicians who are given the same kind of freedom as rock musicians 
are cats like Herbie Hancock and Chick Corea. It's hard to tell them what to play 
because more often than not their producers are not up to their level musically and 
they really don't understand what they are trying to do. Since the direction is so new, 
they just don't know how to handle it." 
barry taylor
